result: The authors performed a high-throughput screen of 4730 compounds using an optogenetic TopBP1 system, identifying >300 potential TopBP1 condensation inhibitors. From 131 selected compounds, 10 were identified as most effective at inhibiting Chk1 phosphorylation, with AZD2858 showing the strongest synergistic interaction with FOLFIRI and efficacy at 1 µM.
evaluation: All reviewers accepted the screening approach and findings. Reviewer 2 described the screen as using 'a high throughput screen of 4730 existing or candidate small molecule anti-cancer drugs' and noted the selection process without criticism. Reviewer 1 confirmed 'The requested plots are in figure S7 of the latest manuscript version, and look convincing,' indicating acceptance of the screening data.

result: AZD2858 disrupted TopBP1 assembly induced by SN-38, resulting in significant reduction in the number of endogenous TopBP1 condensates per nucleus and severely reduced ATR signaling induction as indicated by decreased Chk1 phosphorylation at S345 and RPA32 phosphorylation at S33.
evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirmed these findings. The editor stated 'This valuable study reveals that the GSK-3 inhibitor AZD2858 inhibits the formation of TOPBP1 condensates.' Reviewer 2 noted 'AZD2858 is shown to suppress the formation of Topbp1 (endogenous) condensates in cells exposed to SN-38, and to inhibit activation of Chk1' without raising concerns about the data quality or interpretation.

result: Co-incubation of AZD2858 with SN-38 or FOLFIRI did not affect the ATM pathway (unchanged ATM phosphorylation at S1981 and Chk2 phosphorylation at T68) and did not affect γH2AX levels at early time points (2 hours), demonstrating pathway specificity.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly confirmed this selectivity: 'AZD2858 therefore seems to selectively inhibit the Topbp1-ATR-Chk1 pathway without interfering with parallel branches of the DNA damage signalling system, consistent with Topbp1 condensation being the primary target.' No reviewer challenged these specificity claims.

result: Although AZD2858 is a known GSK-3β inhibitor, its modulation of the ATR/Chk1 pathway is independent of GSK-3β activity. This was demonstrated by: (1) comparable Chk1 phosphorylation in GSK3-β-depleted and control cells, (2) maintained Chk1 inhibition by AZD2858 in GSK3-β-depleted cells, (3) no significant increase in GSK-3β phosphorylation at S9 with the combination, and (4) lack of effect by other more specific GSK-3β inhibitors on TopBP1 condensation.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly validated this mechanism: 'neither siRNA depletion of GSK3-beta, or other GSK3-beta inhibitors were able to recapitulate this effect, suggesting it was a specific non-canonical effect of AZD2858 and not a consequence of GSK3-beta inhibition per se.' The editor noted the evidence is 'convincing.' No reviewer questioned these mechanistic conclusions.

result: AZD2858 disrupts TopBP1 self-interaction and binding to ATR in mammalian cells, as demonstrated by TurboID proximity labeling showing drastic reduction in TopBP1 proximity with recombinant and endogenous TopBP1 and with ATR upon AZD2858 incubation.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 acknowledged this mechanism without criticism, and Reviewer 3 summarized 'disrupting TOPBP1 assembly inhibits the ATR/Chk1 signaling pathway' as a key finding. No reviewer challenged the TurboID data or the interpretation of disrupted protein-protein interactions.

result: In cell-free Xenopus laevis egg extracts, combining CPT and AZD2858 enhanced the accumulation of replication-related factors (RPA, TopBP1, and Pol ε) on chromatin compared to CPT alone, particularly at 60 min after starting replication, possibly due to increased origin activation when the S-phase checkpoint is inhibited.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted the Xenopus extract data without criticism. Reviewer 2 noted the use of 'cell-free Xenopus laevis egg extracts' as part of the experimental approach. The editor noted the evidence is 'convincing,' and no concerns were raised about this orthogonal system or its interpretation.

result: AZD2858 combined with SN-38 affects replication fork progression and disrupts cell cycle homeostasis by inhibiting the ATR/Chk1 signaling pathway. This is evidenced by: (1) partially reduced BrdU incorporation with the combination, (2) significantly reduced negative impact on replication fork progression (DNA fiber analysis), and (3) weakening of the SN-38-induced S-phase checkpoint after 6-12 hours of co-treatment.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly confirmed these findings: 'SN-38 treatment of HCT116 cells markedly suppresses DNA replication, however this was partially reversed by co-treatment with AZD2858, consistent with the failure to activate ATR-Chk1 conferring a defect in replication checkpoint function.' No reviewer questioned the cell cycle or DNA fiber data.

result: The combination of SN-38 and AZD2858 attenuates the S-phase checkpoint, thereby activating a compensatory post-replicative cell cycle checkpoint that arrests the cell cycle before mitosis, as shown by increased cells transitioning into S-phase and progressive accumulation of BrdU-positive cells with 4N DNA content in G2 phase.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this interpretation of the cell cycle data. Reviewer 2 noted the combination 'conferring a defect in replication checkpoint function' without challenging the compensatory checkpoint interpretation. No reviewer raised concerns about this mechanistic model.

result: The AZD2858 and SN-38 combination disrupts TopBP1 assembly, inhibiting ATR kinase activity amplification, leading to elevated DSBs and increased γH2AX and cleaved PARP1 levels at later time points, indicating impaired DNA damage repair and checkpoint regulation.
evaluation: Reviewer 3 summarized the key finding as 'disrupting TOPBP1 assembly inhibits the ATR/Chk1 signaling pathway, leading to increased DNA damage and apoptosis.' Reviewer 2 noted the combination leads to 'increased apoptosis and growth arrest' without questioning the DNA damage data. The editor found the evidence 'convincing.'

result: AZD2858 prevented S-phase checkpoint induction by SN-38, leading to increased DNA damage and apoptosis in colorectal cancer cells. After 48 hr incubation with sublethal doses, the sub-G1 population increased by 40%, and combined treatments led to increased cleaved PARP1, cleaved caspase-3, and DNA DSB accumulation, with synergistic inhibition of cell survival.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 explicitly confirmed: 'Figures 4 and 5 demonstrate that AZD2858 can markedly enhance the cytotoxic and cytostatic effects of SN-38 and FOLFIRI through a combination of increased apoptosis and growth arrest.' Reviewer 3 noted 'leading to increased DNA damage and apoptosis' as a key finding. No concerns were raised about the apoptosis data.

result: AZD2858 showed synergistic effects in combination with FOLFIRI in multiple colorectal cancer cell lines in both 2D and 3D spheroid models. The combination was cytostatic at low doses and cytotoxic at higher doses, with nearly complete elimination of spheroids in all tested cell lines, demonstrating remarkable efficacy.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 noted 'Figure 6 extends this analysis to cells cultured as spheroids, sometimes considered to better represent tumor responses compared to single cell cultures' without criticism. Reviewer 3 confirmed the identification of AZD2858 'which inhibits TOPBP1 condensation and works synergistically with first-line chemotherapy to suppress colorectal cancer cell growth.' The editor found the work 'valuable.'

result: No synergistic effect was observed on CCD 841 CoN normal colon cells with the AZD2858 and FOLFIRI combination, suggesting potential selectivity for cancer cells.
evaluation: Reviewer 2 noted this is 'an important point with respect to the possible practical application of this combination for cancer therapy, however this seems somewhat subsidiary to the main novelty and significance of the findings.' This suggests the reviewer found the data present but insufficient to fully establish therapeutic selectivity, though not critical to the main conclusions.

result: The FOLFIRI+AZD2858 combination was synergistic in SN-38-resistant cell lines (HCT116 SN-6 and HCT116 SN-50), which have increased TopBP1 condensates, indicating that this combination may alleviate drug resistance in colorectal cancer.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted these findings without criticism. Reviewer 3 noted the effects occur 'even in drug-resistant colorectal cancer cell lines' as a key finding. No reviewer questioned the resistance model data or the interpretation regarding potential to overcome resistance.

result: AZD2858 co-incubation led to decreased 53BP1 foci but did not modulate PML nuclear bodies, demonstrating selectivity for certain condensate types.
evaluation: Reviewers did not challenge these specificity controls. The data on 53BP1 and PML bodies were presented as controls to demonstrate selectivity, and no reviewer raised concerns about these findings or their interpretation.

result: A significantly higher number of TopBP1 foci was observed in HCT116-SN50 cells (50-fold more resistant to SN-38) compared to parental HCT116 cells, suggesting a relationship between TopBP1 condensates and drug resistance.
evaluation: Reviewers accepted this observation as part of the rationale for targeting TopBP1 condensates in resistant cells. No concerns were raised about this comparative analysis or its implications for the study design.
